diagnostic_evidence.quote: hence AO is guaranteed to have a subsequence converging to a critical pair
if it is a critical pair such that it is neither local maxima nor local minima

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract claims the heuristics compute locally optimal solutions, but the only formal convergence result (Grippo--Sciandrone) guarantees convergence of a subsequence to a critical (stationary) pair. The paper itself defines saddle points as critical pairs that are neither local maxima nor local minima, so critical points need not be locally optimal. The formal content supports only convergence to critical points.

failure_location.quote: The other two are heuristics, meaning that they rapidly compute locally optimal solutions

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'locally optimal solutions' with 'critical points' or 'stationary points' in the abstract.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised output quality of the two heuristic algorithms (E-AO and SRPL) is overstated; only convergence to critical points is established, not to local optima.
issues.title: Abstract overclaims heuristic output as locally optimal solutions
issues.why_classification: A short local wording change in the abstract preserves every formal claim and guarantee; no proof, lemma, or algorithm is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the optimal value of $\SV(A,P,Q)$ is the minimum entry of $G^\top AH$

issues.failure_explanation: When P and Q each have one generator, the optimal value equals (G^T AH)_{11}. For this to equal ||A|| one needs (G^T AH)_{11} = ||A||, not merely (G^T AH)_{11} >= 0. Counterexample: A = diag(0,1), P = Q = R_+ e_1 gives G^T AH = [0] (nonnegative) but optimal value 0 != 1 = ||A||. The stated condition is necessary but not sufficient.

failure_location.quote: it is equivalent to say that both $P,Q$ have only one generator and $G^\top AH$ is a $1\times 1$ nonnegative matrix.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the condition from 'G^T AH is a 1x1 nonnegative matrix' to '(G^T AH)_{11} = ||A||'.
issues.overall_effect: The stated test for the exclusion case in Corollary cor:saddle_ConeSV is too permissive; a reader may wrongly believe the saddle-point exclusion fails when the optimal value is merely nonnegative but strictly less than ||A||.
issues.title: False equivalence for detecting the case angle(u,Av) = ||A||
issues.why_classification: A short local correction to a prose passage; all formal results and guarantees survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The construction of V requires forming A_x U / lambda where lambda = -sqrt(rho(A_y A_x)). When rho(A_y A_x) = 0 (which occurs when A_y A_x = 0, since it is similar to a PSD matrix), lambda = 0 and the expression A_x U / lambda is undefined (division by zero). The proposition does not state the hypothesis rho(A_y A_x) > 0 that the construction requires.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis rho(A_yA_x) > 0 to the proposition, or handle the degenerate case separately by using ker(M) as the relevant eigenspace when lambda = 0.
issues.overall_effect: Items 3 and 4 of Proposition pro:sufficient_conditions_feasibility are ill-defined when rho(A_yA_x) = 0; the feasibility test cannot be carried out in this degenerate case.
issues.title: Construction of V is undefined when spectral radius is zero
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard local condition (or fixing the degenerate case) preserves the method, conclusion, and algorithm (which already skips rho = 0 via its skip test).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and $\mu$ are nonzero, then $A_yA_x w_x = \mu A_y w_y = \mu^2 w_x$

issues.failure_explanation: The derivation in the proof only establishes the eigenvalue correspondence for nonzero eigenvalues of M (the proof explicitly assumes mu is nonzero). When A_yA_x has 0 as an eigenvalue, the left-hand side of the displayed equation includes 0 (from lambda = 0 in Lambda(A_yA_x)) while the right-hand side excludes 0 by definition. The correct equation should use Lambda(A_yA_x) minus {0} on the left-hand side.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the left-hand side to restrict to nonzero eigenvalues of A_yA_x, matching the derivation that only covers mu != 0.
issues.overall_effect: The display equation is false when A_yA_x is singular. The conclusion it supports (that -sqrt(rho(A_yA_x)) is the least eigenvalue of M) remains correct despite this error.
issues.title: Eigenvalue correspondence display equation is incorrect at zero
issues.why_classification: A short local correction to a display equation in the proof preserves the proposition's conclusion and all downstream results.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated substitution x = a/sqrt(2n) gives ||x||^2 = ||a||^2/(2n) = 1/(4n^2) != 1, contradicting the claimed constraint ||x||^2 = 1. The correct substitution is x = a*sqrt(2n) (equivalently a = x/sqrt(2n)). The same inversion appears in the reconstruction formula 'a = sqrt(2n) x' which should be 'a = x/sqrt(2n)'. With the corrected substitution the chain of equalities and the matrix M are correct.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change x = a/sqrt(2n) to x = a*sqrt(2n) and y = lambda/sqrt(2) to y = lambda*sqrt(2), and correspondingly the reconstruction formulas to a = x/sqrt(2n) and lambda = y/sqrt(2).
issues.overall_effect: Following the stated change of variables and reconstruction formulas yields matrices P and N with incorrect Frobenius norms. The lemma's equivalence claim between MA(CP_n, CN_n) and PSV(M) remains correct with the corrected substitution.
issues.title: Change of variables in Lemma is inverted
issues.why_classification: The repair is a forced correction of an inverted factor in the substitution and its inverse; the lemma statement and proof content survive with the corrected substitution.
